reason: The rough edge is the visible cause of the skin and vessel break, so the body needs to encounter it first.
expectation: The body will sustain a small cut, making the bleeding response possible.

effect: The cut and narrowed vessel establish the injury; platelets are the next apparent part of stopping the leak.
reaction: The vessel narrowing is a useful early detail.
reason: Platelets at the cut should help form an initial plug in the damaged vessel.
expectation: Platelets will gather at the damaged vessel and begin forming a plug.

effect: The platelet plug slows the leak; clotting factors and fibrinogen may help reinforce it.
reaction: The distinction between slowing the leak and securing the clot is useful.
reason: Activated clotting factors should act on soluble fibrinogen to form fibrin.
expectation: Fibrinogen will be converted into fibrin for the clot.

effect: Fibrinogen has become fibrin threads, ready to reinforce the platelet plug.
reaction: The thread mesh makes the reinforcement easy to picture.
reason: The fibrin mesh should strengthen the plug at the vessel break.
expectation: The threads will reinforce the platelet plug and stop the bleeding.

effect: The fibrin mesh sealed the vessel and stopped bleeding, but the skin remains open; stopping the leak is distinct from tissue repair.
reaction: The distinction between a sealed vessel and an open wound is a useful ending.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reinforcing the platelet plug with fibrin made the separate roles of platelets and the mesh clear, while showing that the skin still needs repair.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making fibrin threads was visually useful, but the planned picture and prose did not explain how the activated clotting factors convert fibrinogen into fibrin.

surprise.text: The injured vessel was already narrowed before the platelet plug formed, adding an early response I had not expected.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the activated clotting factors appeared without an explanation of how they became active.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how the still-open skin repairs after the bleeding stops; this chapter made that next question clear.
